governance.note: FORWARD-SKILL validation of the gas-elastic neighbor heat rate (G11). The new lever is the _HR_GAS_ELASTIC map in market_sim.data.neighbor_price (keyed by neighbor name) for MISO's PJM and SPP seams: the FORWARD neighbor implied HR is HR(gas)=hr_phys+hr_adder/gas, an OLS fit of each neighbor's OWN measured (Henry Hub, realized RT LMP) points (scripts/derive_neighbor_hr_elasticity.py; PJM 11.06*gas+3.21, SPP 3.04*gas+16.27). It replaces the flat multi-year-mean marginal_heat_rate for forecast years. The fit is BLIND to MISO's interchange (rule #11) - it reads only the neighbor's price and Henry Hub. Backcast keepers still price off the measured hr_by_year anchor (rule #12); this run sets MARKET_SIM_NEIGHBOR_HR_FORWARD_SKILL to force the seam onto the FORWARD path so the forward formula is scored against held-out actuals vs the old flat mean - no input is rescaled to a MISO output residual, no unit pinned to CEMS. All other MISO levers unchanged (priced reference-price node, Manitoba firm-hydro, per-plant CAMPD bins, historic CAMPD unit-outage windows = exogenous availability, F923 monthly delivered fuel).
governance.open_misses_note: Net interchange TWh (actual | flat-fwd | elastic-fwd): 2023 -37.9|-56.0|-57.2; 2024 -23.1|-64.2|-59.9; 2025 -19.0|+4.8(flat export-flip)|-9.5. The elastic HR fixes the dear-gas 2025 SPP sign-flip (flat over-prices wind-set SPP at HR 10.0 -> spurious net export; elastic collapses SPP to 7.66=measured -> net import restored, RMSE 3440->1866) and eases the 2024 over-import (RMSE 5006->4573); 2023 ~neutral (+1.1 TWh over-import, RMSE +1.8%). Mean interchange RMSE 3681->3028 (-18%). NOT a keeper replacing miso-9 (its measured-anchor backcast is byte-identical). Open structural misses unchanged from miso-9: import-node over-serves (the -56/-60 TWh 2023/24 over-import is the import-node lever, not the HR); CT_PEAKER under-dispatch; scarcity tail absent. These are the next levers, not residual fits.
